newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies inviting Israeli fencers to event.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies inviting Israeli fencers to event.

text.p: Iran has denied inviting athletes from its arch-foe Israel to attend an international fencing tournament in Tehran, a newspaper said on Monday.

The daily Johuri Eslami quoted Iran's fencing federation as denying it had invited Israel to the event due to be held next month as part of games marking Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution. It suggested the invitation might have been extended by the Paris-based International Fencing Federation.
Israeli fencing federation director Moshe Ben-Ezra said on Sunday he had received an invitation from the head of the Tehran event in an envelope of the International Fencing Organisation.
"Athletes from the Islamic Republic have refused repeatedly to compete against fencers of the regime (Israel) occupying Qods (Jerusalem)," the newspaper quoted the Iranian federation as saying.
"This federation is a drop of the unending ocean of the Moslem people and it works within the framework of the rules and policies of the Islamic Republic."
Iran says Israel has no right to exist. Tehran strongly opposes the Middle East peace process as a sell-out of Palestinian and Arab rights.
